title: Simple Graph Structure
content: Custom `SimpleG n` structure for graphs on $\text{Fin}\,n$ vertices, with adjacency relation `adj`, symmetry, and irreflexivity. This avoids Mathlib's `SimpleGraph` type class complexity while maintaining the essential properties needed for Ramsey theory. The structure is parameterized by vertex count $n$.
mathContext: `SimpleG n` = $(V, E)$ with $V = \text{Fin}\,n$, $E \subseteq \binom{V}{2}$, formalized as `adj : Fin n \to Fin n \to Prop` with `symm` and `irrefl`

title: Clique Definition
content: A $k$-clique in $G$ is a subset $S$ of $k$ vertices where every pair is adjacent. This is the combinatorial heart of Ramsey theory: $R(k)$ is the minimum $n$ forcing a $k$-clique or $k$-independent set in every graph on $n$ vertices.
mathContext: $G.\text{hasClique}(k) \iff \exists S \subseteq V, |S| = k, \forall u, v \in S, u \ne v \Rightarrow G.\text{adj}(u, v)$

title: Independent Set Definition
content: A $k$-independent set in $G$ is a subset $S$ of $k$ vertices where no pair is adjacent. Equivalently, it is a $k$-clique in the complement graph $\overline{G}$. The independence number $\alpha(G)$ is the size of the largest independent set.
mathContext: $G.\text{hasIndepSet}(k) \iff \exists S \subseteq V, |S| = k, \forall u, v \in S, u \ne v \Rightarrow \neg G.\text{adj}(u, v)$

title: Diagonal Ramsey Number R(k)
content: The diagonal Ramsey number $R(k)$ is the minimum $n$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices contains either a $k$-clique or a $k$-independent set. Equivalently, every 2-coloring of $K_n$'s edges contains a monochromatic $K_k$. The axiomatization separates the existence (`ramseyNumber`) from the specification (`ramseyNumber_spec`), which states the Ramsey property for graphs on $R(k)$ vertices.
mathContext: $R(k) = \min\{n : \forall G \text{ on } n \text{ vertices}, \omega(G) \ge k \text{ or } \alpha(G) \ge k\}$

title: Erdős Probabilistic Bound (1947)
content: Erdős's landmark 1947 result: $R(k) > k \cdot 2^{k/2} / e$, proved by showing a random graph on $n < \sqrt{2}^k$ vertices has no $k$-clique or $k$-independent set with positive probability. This was the birth of the probabilistic method in combinatorics. The bound is non-constructive: it proves existence without giving an explicit construction. The formalization axiomatizes both the exponential form ($\exists C > 1, C^k \le R(k)$) and the asymptotic $\sqrt{2}$ constant.
mathContext: $R(k) \ge k \cdot 2^{k/2}/e \approx (\sqrt{2})^k$. Proof: $\Pr[\text{random } G \text{ has } k\text{-clique}] \le \binom{n}{k} 2^{-\binom{k}{2}} < 1$ when $n < \sqrt{2}^k$

title: Explicit Construction Predicate
content: The predicate `IsExplicit G` is axiomatized as `True` since constructibility is a meta-property (polynomial-time computability of the adjacency function). The key requirement for Problem #78 is that the graph can be constructed in $\text{poly}(n)$ time, not just shown to exist probabilistically. This connects to circuit complexity and derandomization.
mathContext: A graph is explicit if $\text{adj}(u, v)$ is computable in $\text{poly}(\log n)$ time

title: Cohen's Construction (2015)
content: Cohen (2015) built explicit $n$-vertex graphs with no clique or independent set of size $2^{(\log \log n)^C}$. This was the first super-polylogarithmic improvement over trivial algebraic constructions but still exponentially far from the target $c \cdot \log n$. The construction uses algebraic geometry and character sum estimates.
mathContext: $\alpha(G), \omega(G) < 2^{(\log \log n)^C}$ — doubly logarithmic, far from the target $O(\log n)$

title: Li's Construction (2023)
content: Li (2023) improved the explicit construction to achieve $\alpha(G), \omega(G) < (\log n)^C$. This is the current state of the art for constructive Ramsey bounds. The gap from $(\log n)^C$ to the target $c \cdot \log n$ (polynomial in $\log n$ vs. linear in $\log n$) remains enormous and represents a fundamental barrier in combinatorics.
mathContext: Li: $\alpha(G), \omega(G) < (\log n)^C$ vs. target $c \cdot \log n$ — a polynomial-vs-linear gap in $\log n$

title: Constructive Ramsey Challenge ($100)
content: The main open problem: construct explicit $n$-vertex graphs with no clique or independent set of size $c \cdot \log n$. This would match the probabilistic lower bound constructively, showing $R(k) > C^k$ for an explicit family. Erdős offered $\$100$ for this. The formalization axiomatizes the existence of such a constant $c > 0$ and an explicit graph family.
mathContext: $\exists c > 0, \forall n \ge 2, \exists G$ explicit on $n$ vertices: $\omega(G), \alpha(G) < c \cdot \log n$

title: Erdős–Szekeres Upper Bound (1935)
content: The classical Erdős–Szekeres bound $R(k) \le \binom{2k-2}{k-1} < 4^k$ from 1935 was the first explicit upper bound on diagonal Ramsey numbers. The proof uses the recurrence $R(r,s) \le R(r-1,s) + R(r,s-1)$ and induction. This $4^k$ barrier stood for nearly 90 years.

title: CGMS Upper Bound (2023)
content: Campos, Griffiths, Morris, and Sahasrabudhe (2023) proved $R(k) \le (4 - \varepsilon)^k$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, breaking the 88-year-old $4^k$ barrier. Their proof uses a novel graph coloring algorithm with entropy compression. This was one of the biggest breakthroughs in Ramsey theory and narrows the gap between upper and lower bounds.

title: Paley Graph and the Constructive Gap
content: The best known explicit Ramsey graphs before Li (2023) were Paley graphs: for a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, connect vertices $i, j \in \mathbb{F}_p$ iff $i - j$ is a quadratic residue. These achieve $\alpha(G), \omega(G) \sim \sqrt{p}$ (by the Weil bound), giving independence/clique number $\sqrt{n}$. The target is $c \cdot \log n$, an exponential gap from $\sqrt{n}$. This gap between $\sqrt{n}$ and $\log n$ represents one of the largest known gaps between constructive and probabilistic bounds in all of combinatorics.
mathContext: Paley graph: $\omega(G), \alpha(G) \sim \sqrt{n}$ vs. target $c \cdot \log n$ — an exponential gap
